title: Analyzing the hate and counter speech accounts on Twitter
findings: Hate speech targeting religious groups constitutes the largest fraction (23.6%) of hateful tweets in the dataset and receives the highest average number of counterspeech replies (4.9 per tweet). Counterspeakers responding to religious hate speech are more likely to use strategies like 'presentation of facts' and 'pointing out hypocrisy' and are least likely to use hostile language compared to counterspeech against other communities.
references: Badjatiya, P.; Gupta, S.; Gupta, M.; and Varma, V. 2017. Deep learning for hate speech detection in tweets. WWW, 759-760.
